---
title: Your first video with curl
description: Upload a file, wait for it to encode and play it, using nothing but curl and jq against the API.
icon: Terminal
---

This page walks one video through the API by hand: you create an upload with
your API key, send the file in parts straight to storage, tell ClipMux the
upload is complete, wait until the video is ready, and play its
`master.m3u8`. It's the same sequence the SDK and `<clipmux-uploader>` run
for you, so it's worth doing once to see what they do.

Every request and response here is in the
[API reference](/docs/reference/api/uploads).

## Before you start

- A ClipMux server, for example `https://video.example.com`. To run one, see
  [Install with one line](/docs/self-host/install).
- An API key for an app, `cmx_…`, with the default scopes (`uploads:write`,
  `assets:read`, `assets:write`). `npx @clipmux/node init` writes one to
  `.env.local`; you can also create one under **Apps & API** in the
  dashboard, or with `clipmux admin create-key --app NAME` on the server.
- `curl`, `jq` and a short video file, here `lesson-42.mp4`.

```bash
export CLIPMUX_URL=https://video.example.com
export CLIPMUX_API_KEY=cmx_…
FILE=lesson-42.mp4
```

<Warning>
  The API key is a secret. Use it from a terminal or your backend, never in
  browser code. The browser side of an upload uses the upload token, which
  reaches only that one upload.
</Warning>

## Upload and play

<Steps>
<Step>

### Create the upload

Send the file's size in bytes. `passthrough` is your own ID for the video
and `title` is a name for people; both are optional.

```bash
SIZE=$(wc -c < "$FILE" | tr -d ' ')

curl -s "$CLIPMUX_URL/v1/uploads" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"size\": $SIZE, \"passthrough\": \"lesson_42\", \"title\": \"Lesson 42\"}" \
  | tee upload.json
```

```json
{
  "upload_id": "upl_…",
  "asset_id": "ast_…",
  "part_size": 33554432,
  "part_count": 22,
  "upload_token": "M4XQ7R2VK6WT5ZJYBNC3D4F7GH",
  "playback_ids": [{ "id": "pid_…", "policy": "signed", "playable": false, "status": "active" }]
}
```

The video exists at once, as `ast_…` in `waiting_upload`, with a private
(`signed`) playback ID you can store before the file arrives. Every part is
`part_size` bytes (32 MiB) except the last.

```bash
UPLOAD_ID=$(jq -r .upload_id upload.json)
ASSET_ID=$(jq -r .asset_id upload.json)
UPLOAD_TOKEN=$(jq -r .upload_token upload.json)
PART_SIZE=$(jq -r .part_size upload.json)
PART_COUNT=$(jq -r .part_count upload.json)
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Send the parts

For each part, ask ClipMux for a signed URL with the upload token, `PUT` the
part's bytes to it, and keep the `ETag` header storage answers with. You can
sign up to 100 part numbers in one call, and each URL lasts an hour; this
loop signs one part at a time to keep it short.

```bash
echo '[]' > parts.json
for n in $(seq 1 "$PART_COUNT"); do
  URL=$(curl -s "$CLIPMUX_URL/v1/uploads/$UPLOAD_ID/parts" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $UPLOAD_TOKEN" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"part_numbers\": [$n]}" | jq -r '.parts[0].url')
  dd if="$FILE" of=part.bin bs="$PART_SIZE" skip=$((n - 1)) count=1 2>/dev/null
  ETAG=$(curl -s -T part.bin -D - -o /dev/null "$URL" \
    | grep -i '^etag:' | cut -d' ' -f2 | tr -d '\r')
  jq --argjson n "$n" --arg etag "$ETAG" \
    '. + [{part_number: $n, etag: $etag}]' parts.json > parts.tmp && mv parts.tmp parts.json
done
rm part.bin
```

The parts go straight to storage, not through your backend. If the loop
stops halfway, `GET /v1/uploads/{id}/parts` with the upload token lists the
parts storage already holds, so you send only the rest. An upload left idle
for 24 hours expires.

</Step>
<Step>

### Complete the upload

Send every part's number and `ETag`:

```bash
jq '{parts: .}' parts.json | curl -s "$CLIPMUX_URL/v1/uploads/$UPLOAD_ID/complete" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $UPLOAD_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d @- | jq '{id, status}'
```

The answer is the video, now `processing`. Encoding has started.

</Step>
<Step>

### Wait until it's ready

Ask for the video until its status moves on from `processing`:

```bash
while :; do
  STATUS=$(curl -s "$CLIPMUX_URL/v1/assets/$ASSET_ID" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY" | jq -r .status)
  echo "$STATUS"
  [ "$STATUS" = processing ] || break
  sleep 10
done
```

It ends `ready`, or `errored` with an `error_code` saying why. In an app,
don't poll: ClipMux sends `video.asset.ready` to your webhook endpoint. See
[Receive webhooks](/docs/build/webhooks).

</Step>
<Step>

### Play it

Get the playback ID and the media origin, `base_url`, from the video:

```bash
curl -s "$CLIPMUX_URL/v1/assets/$ASSET_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY" > asset.json
PLAYBACK_ID=$(jq -r '.playback_ids[0].id' asset.json)
BASE_URL=$(jq -r .base_url asset.json)
```

The video is private, so it plays only with a token: a short JWT your
backend signs with your app's signing key. Sign one as
[Sign playback tokens](/docs/build/play/sign-tokens) shows, in Node, Python,
Go or PHP, and put it in `TOKEN`. Then:

```bash
echo "$BASE_URL/v/$TOKEN/$PLAYBACK_ID/master.m3u8"
```

Safari plays that URL directly, and so does
[`<clipmux-player>`](/docs/build/play/player).

To skip the token for a throwaway test, create the upload with
`"playback_policy": "public"`. Anyone with the URL can then watch it at
`$BASE_URL/p/$PLAYBACK_ID/master.m3u8`. See
[Public videos](/docs/build/play/public-videos).

</Step>
</Steps>

## Check it works

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "$BASE_URL/v/$TOKEN/$PLAYBACK_ID/master.m3u8"
```

`200` means the video plays. If a step failed, the error's `code` says why:

- `401 unauthorized` on create: the API key is wrong or revoked.
- `403 insufficient_scope`: the key lacks `uploads:write` (create) or
  `assets:read` (the status loop).
- `413 too_large`: the file is over this server's upload limit. See
  [Limits and defaults](/docs/reference/limits).
- `400 invalid_parts` on complete: an `ETag` is missing or wrong, usually
  because a `PUT` failed. Check `parts.json` for an empty `etag`, send that
  part again and complete again.
- `409 upload_expired`: the upload sat idle for 24 hours. Create a new one.
- The status ends `errored`: `error_code` says why, for example
  `unsupported_source` for a file that isn't a video ClipMux can read.
- `401 token_expired` or `403 denied` when playing: the token is expired or
  wrong. See [Sign playback tokens](/docs/build/play/sign-tokens).

Every code is in [Errors](/docs/reference/errors).
